title: One Registry to Rule them All - Sonny Merla, Mauro Luchetti, & Mattia Redaelli, Quantyca

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk presents an enterprise developer platform combining an AI gateway, MCP/A2A/use-case registries, template repositories, and CI/CD publishing that other teams build on. Amplifon's Amplify program is internal enterprise infrastructure serving distributed software teams across 26 countries. The platform is actively under development with six demo entities and is preparing for production deployment but not yet in full production. The talk assumes prior familiarity with MCP, A2A, Entra ID, GitHub Actions, FastAPI, and Docker. Recorded conference talk with slide-based UI walkthroughs and CI/CD pipeline diagrams. Ten grounded evidence anchors with verbatim excerpts and character offsets support each key claim.

summary: Amplifon, operating across 26 countries with over 20,000 employees and 10,000 stores, launched the Amplify program in January 2025 to standardize AI adoption. The program features an operating model with a control tower (setting guidelines for security, legal, technology, and strategy) and a committee (running strategy across countries and corporate). Three focus areas are governance, platform, and factory. Key organizational problems include short LLM lifecycle maintenance, governance and compliance needs requiring asset catalogs and lineage, and enterprise scaling across distributed teams. The technical solution starts with an AI gateway providing unified model access, Entra ID authentication, budgeting controls, and central auditing/monitoring. Three registries were built on top. The private MCP registry extends the public community registry with enterprise metadata including ownership, environment, authentication model, cost attribution, and use case linkage, enabling impact analysis and auditability. The A2A registry uses agent cards describing agent identity, endpoints, capabilities, modalities, and authentication; agents auto-publish their cards via CI/CD. The use case registry connects MCP servers and A2A agents to specific business use cases, tracking assets, models, deployment systems, and inter-use-case relationships. The platform UI provides use case detail views showing status, version, description, assets, AI models, and lifecycle history; a catalog view of use cases, MCP servers, and A2A agents; inspector pages for testing MCP servers and validating A2A agent card compatibility; form-based widgets for generating server.json and agent cards with preview; and a lineage view visualizing connections between use cases, agents, and models with outage impact tracing. For enterprise development, two GitHub template repositories (one for MCP, one for A2A) provide boilerplate, Dockerfiles, package management, FastAPI server structure, authentication, and cost tracking. The A2A blueprint is framework-agnostic, using interfaces and ports so teams can use LangChain, Agno, or any framework while exposing a standard interface. LangFuse is integrated at the platform level for agent tracing, evaluation, and performance monitoring. CI/CD pipelines publish Docker images to an artifact repository and metadata (agent cards, server.json) to the registry backend. Runtime discovery works through AI gateway proxies that look up the catalog to resolve backend URLs, with agents authenticating via additional headers. The platform is preparing for production deployment and remains under active development.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Amplifon Context
sections.summary: Sonny Merla introduces the problem of chaotic AI development across dozens of teams and continents. Amplifon is described as a global hearing care leader in 26 countries with 20,000+ employees and 10,000+ stores, currently undergoing AI transformation.

sections.title: Amplify Program Operating Model
sections.summary: The Amplify program (launched January 2025) is described with its operating model: a control tower setting guidelines and strategy, and a committee running strategy across countries. Three focus areas are governance, platform, and factory.

sections.title: Organizational Challenges for AI at Scale
sections.summary: Key problems include maintenance and operations (short LLM lifecycles), governance and compliance (need for catalogs and lineage), and enterprise scaling (centralized governance with reusable guidelines across teams and infrastructures).

sections.title: AI Gateway and Three Registries Overview
sections.summary: Mauro introduces the AI gateway (unified access, Entra ID auth, budgeting, auditing) and three registries: MCP registry (tool catalog), A2A registry (agent catalog using agent cards), and use case registry (linking metadata for governance and lineage).

sections.title: Private MCP Registry Details
sections.summary: The private MCP registry extends the public community registry with custom internal servers and curated public servers, enriched with enterprise metadata: ownership, environment, authentication model, cost attribution, and use case linkage enabling impact analysis and auditability.

sections.title: A2A Registry and Use Case Registry
sections.summary: The A2A registry uses agent cards describing identity, endpoints, capabilities, modalities, and auth; agents auto-publish cards via CI/CD. The use case registry maps agents and tools to specific use cases, tracking assets, models, deployment systems, and inter-use-case connections.

sections.title: Platform Walkthrough
sections.summary: Brief platform UI demo showing home page, catalog (use cases, MCP, A2A agents), and AI gateway section. The platform is preparing for production with six demo entities currently defined.

sections.title: Use Case Detail, Inspector, Widgets, and Lineage Views
sections.summary: Detailed UI walkthrough showing use case pages with status, version, description, assets, AI models, and lifecycle history. MCP server and A2A agent detail pages display server.json and agent card content respectively. Inspector pages allow testing MCP servers and validating A2A agent card compatibility. Form-based widgets generate server.json and agent cards with preview. Lineage views visualize use case connections to agents and models, enabling outage impact tracing.

sections.title: Enterprise Development Cycle and Template Repositories
sections.summary: Two GitHub template repositories (one for MCP, one for A2A) provide boilerplate, Dockerfiles, package management, FastAPI server structure, authentication, and cost tracking. LangFuse is integrated at platform level for observability. The A2A blueprint is framework-agnostic using interfaces and ports so teams can choose LangChain, Agno, or any framework while exposing a standard interface.

sections.title: CI/CD Pipeline and Runtime Discovery
sections.summary: CI/CD pipelines triggered by tagging a branch publish Docker images to an artifact repository and metadata (agent cards, server.json) to the registry backend proxy. Runtime discovery works through AI gateway proxies that look up the catalog to resolve backend URLs, with agents authenticating via additional headers. The talk concludes with a business summary emphasizing governance, traceability, standard blueprints, and CI/CD tying deployment to metadata, with ongoing development and invitation for collaboration.
